$comment: Unit prices used to turn MEASURED usage into an estimated cost.
This file is the whole reason the estimate is checkable. Usage is
measured (tokens reported by the model, bytes billed reported by
BigQuery); price is declared here, dated, and cited. The console shows
both, so a reader can recompute the figure or reject the rates.
These are PUBLISHED LIST PRICES for the stated region. They ignore
committed-use discounts, free tiers, sustained-use discounts and any
negotiated rate on the billing account. An estimate built from them is
an upper bound on list, not a prediction of the invoice — which is
exactly why 'Actual cost', sourced from the billing export, is a
separate measurement rather than a refinement of this one.
Re-verify against the source URLs and bump effective_date. The console
displays that date so a stale card is visible rather than silent.

model.$comment: Per 1,000,000 tokens. Keyed by model id; 'default' prices anything unlisted rather than silently costing it at zero.

bigquery_query.$comment: On-demand analysis, per tebibyte BILLED. BigQuery bills a 10 MB minimum per query, which is why bytes_billed is recorded rather than bytes_processed.

bigquery_storage_active.$comment: Active logical storage, per gibibyte-month. Not charged by this project's estimate today - no usage event records storage duration - and present so that a future one is priced from the same place.

bigquery_load.$comment: Batch loads into BigQuery are not charged for the load itself. Recorded explicitly as zero rather than omitted, so a reader can tell a free operation from a forgotten one.
